chats.answer:
A floor-rising projector screen (also called a floor-up projection screen or motorized floor-rising screen) is a projection screen that rises vertically from a compact case placed on the floor or inside a cabinet.

They're especially popular for home theaters because you don't need to mount anything on the wall or ceiling.

What to look for

Motorized vs. manual: Motorized screens rise with a remote; manual screens are usually cheaper.

ALR/CLR material: Ambient-light-rejecting screens are useful in brighter rooms. CLR screens are particularly suited to ultra-short-throw projectors.

Projector compatibility: UST projectors and standard/long-throw projectors often require different screen materials.

Screen size: 100-inch and 120-inch are common home theater sizes.

Tab tensioning: Helps keep the screen flat and reduces wrinkles.

A floor-rising projector screen (also called a floor-up projector screen or motorized floor-rising screen) is a projection screen that rises vertically from a floor-standing enclosure and retracts when not in use.

It's especially popular for home theaters, living rooms, and ultra-short-throw (UST) projectors.

What to look for

Motorized operation: Screen rises and retracts with a remote.

ALR/CLR material: Rejects ambient or ceiling light, especially useful with UST projectors.

Screen size: 100", 110", and 120" are popular choices.

Tab tensioning: Helps maintain a flat projection surface.

Installation: No wall or ceiling mounting required.
